title: Dhurandhar 2 Finally Comes Home to India — and Netflix Is Pouring the 'Raw and Undekha' Cut Straight Into Your Living Room
excerpt: For a month the world got to watch Ranveer Singh's blood-soaked Baloch saga while India was locked out. That ended this week — and the uncut edition lands in five languages, no theatre ticket required.
body:
It is a peculiar kind of torture, watching the whole planet binge a film made in your own language while you sit on your hands. For nearly five weeks, that was the indignity Indian fans of **Dhurandhar: The Revenge** were forced to swallow. The sequel had already conquered cinemas — a reported ₹1,800 crore worldwide, the kind of number that makes trade analysts reach for new adjectives — and then it slipped onto Netflix everywhere *except* the country that crowned it. Pakistan got it. The UAE got it. Mauritius, Bangladesh, Qatar, the Maldives — all No. 1. India? Locked out, scrolling X in envy.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=NHk7scrb_9I</youtube>

That ended this week. Netflix India confirmed the wait was over, and **Dhurandhar: The Revenge — Raw and Undekha** began streaming on June 19, the same Friday Cocktail 2 was busy storming the box office. The diaspora, scattered across time zones and subscription tiers, can finally stop pretending they hadn't already found a way to watch.



> **"The "Raw and Undekha" edition leans into exactly what its name promises: extended sequences, uncensored material, the scenes the theatrical cut couldn't show you."**


https://x.com/ImMeenakshi22/status/2067947821115085071

> "Finally available on Netflix India after JioHotstar!" — the cry that went up across fan forums the moment the announcement dropped

Let us be honest about what this film is. **Aditya Dhar**, who detonated his reputation as a serious commercial director with the first installment, returns with a sequel that is louder, bloodier, and entirely unbothered by your delicate sensibilities. **Ranveer Singh** plays Jaskirat Singh Rangi, an undercover agent who buries his own identity to become Hamza Ali Mazari — *Sher-e-Baloch* — and slithers into Karachi's criminal syndicates to avenge the 26/11 attacks. It is revenge cinema with the safety off. The "Raw and Undekha" edition leans into exactly what its name promises: extended sequences, uncensored material, the scenes the theatrical cut couldn't show you.

What makes Ranveer compelling here isn't the swagger we know him for. It is the disappearance. He doesn't play a hero who happens to go undercover; he plays a man slowly erasing himself, and the film is smart enough to let that erosion show. Around him, the ensemble does serious work — **Sanjay Dutt** and **R. Madhavan** anchor the adult tension, **Rakesh Bedi** turns up as Jameel Jamali, **Arjun Rampal** prowls the margins, and **Akshaye Khanna**, whose character died in part one, makes only a fleeting appearance, a ghost the franchise can't quite let go of.

The numbers tell their own story. The first **Dhurandhar** became a Netflix phenomenon — 29.3 million views, muscling past Crew, Maharaja and Fighter to crack the platform's top ten most-watched Indian films of all time, trailing only RRR, Jawan, Animal, Gangubai Kathiawadi, Laapataa Ladies and Lucky Bhaskar. The sequel arrived globally in May, claimed the No. 1 spot in nine countries in its debut week, and trended across seventeen — all without India in the mix. Now imagine what the domestic numbers do to that tally.

**For the diaspora, this is the good news that matters.** Dhurandhar 2 is streaming on Netflix in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam and Kannada — which means whether you are in Edison or Slough or Brampton, you watch in the language you think in. The split-platform drama that dominated headlines for weeks (Netflix worldwide, JioHotstar at home, India in the middle) has resolved into something clean: it now streams on both JioHotstar and Netflix in India. No regional lockout. No VPN gymnastics. No more watching your cousins in Dubai post spoilers while you wait.

There is a larger signal buried in all this. A Hindi spy thriller about a Balochistan operation, premiering at No. 1 in Pakistan, the UAE and Bangladesh, then conquering Netflix in seventeen countries — that is not a Bollywood story anymore. That is a global one. **Aditya Dhar** set out to make the kind of film that travels without translation, and the streaming charts agree.

So clear your weekend. The most violent, most unapologetic Hindi blockbuster of the year is finally on the platform you already pay for, in the language you already speak. India waited five weeks for its own film. The least you can do is press play.
